site_article.headline: How to use InVideo AI for free: weekly limits, watermarks and how credits work

site_article.seo_title: How to use InVideo AI for free: limits, credits, watermark
site_article.seo_description: How to use InVideo AI for free: the 10 minute weekly limit, 4 exports, the watermark, how paid credits work, and 5 steps to stop wasting your minutes.
site_article.answer_summary: Yes, InVideo AI has a free plan with no card required. It gives 10 minutes of video generation and 4 exports a week, resetting Mondays at 12 a.m. UTC, and every free video has a watermark.

paragraphs.text: You can use InVideo AI for free without entering a card. According to the InVideo help center, the free plan gives you 10 minutes of video generation and 4 exports every week, and that allowance resets every Monday at 12 a.m. UTC.

The catch is the watermark. Every video made and exported on the free plan carries an InVideo watermark plus stock media watermarks, and the only way to remove them is a paid plan. Free videos can still be used and shared on social media, the help center says.
What the InVideo AI free plan includes

The free plan includes unlimited premium stock media from Storyblocks and other stock libraries, according to the help center. Every plan, free included, gets the timeline editor, multiplayer editing and exports. InVideo puts the rule simply: edits and exports are free, while generation and transcripts cost credits.
When you use up the weekly allowance, InVideo shows a "Weekly limit reached" message. Your options are to wait for the Monday reset or to upgrade.
Plan your week around the reset. If you hit the limit on a Friday, you wait until Monday, not 7 days from your first video.
How InVideo credits work

Paid plans run on credits instead of weekly minutes. InVideo's credits page lists Starter with 400 credits a month, Plus with 2,000, Max with 5,000 or 8,000, Max 2x with 10,000, Team with 1,600 per seat and Scale with 4,000 per seat. Enterprise is custom.

Credits pay for video generation with the supported models, premium image, audio and agent work, transcripts and paid stock. They do not pay for editing on the timeline, exporting or downloading something you already generated. Agent Two, InVideo's own agent, uses credits for its work.

The cost depends on the model. InVideo's example: a Kling 2.6 Standard video might cost 5 credits, while a Veo 3.1 video in 4K with audio can cost more than 100. Video models are priced per second, and each generation shows its credit cost before you confirm it.

Plan credits reset on the day of the month you subscribed, also on yearly plans, and unused credits do not roll over. Extra credits bought on top are added right away. InVideo's own pages disagree on how long those last: one says 12 months from purchase, another says they expire after a set period or when your plan ends, whichever comes first.
How to use InVideo AI for free without wasting minutes

paragraphs.title: 1. Sign up on the free plan
paragraphs.text: Create an account without a card. You start with the weekly 10 minutes of generation and 4 exports.

paragraphs.title: 2. Plan the video before you generate
paragraphs.text: InVideo's own advice for bigger projects is to start with a storyboard and have the invideo agent write the prompt for you to review before any generation runs.

paragraphs.title: 3. Turn on Always Ask mode
paragraphs.text: InVideo recommends running the invideo agent in Always Ask mode, so you approve each prompt and reference before anything is spent.

paragraphs.title: 4. Fix things in the editor, not by regenerating
paragraphs.text: Edits on the timeline cost nothing, so trim, reorder and swap stock clips there instead of asking for a new generation.

paragraphs.title: 5. Check what is left
paragraphs.text: Click your profile icon in the top right corner and open the Usage page to see what you have used.
Exports are the tighter limit on the free plan. With 4 a week, finish your edits first and export once.
When the free plan stops being enough

InVideo's own guide to picking a plan, updated in September 2026, says real productions it documented used 3,000 to 30,000 credits per project. Its examples include a 70 second short film that used 3,000 credits and a 2 minute brand promo that used 6,000 to 6,500.

Plan names and prices are not described the same way across InVideo's pages. The credits page lists Starter, Plus, Max, Max 2x, Team and Scale, while the plan guide names Plus, Max, Generative and Elite. Check the pricing page in your own account before you pay.

The free plan works for testing InVideo and for short social clips where a watermark does not matter. For client work, a channel you want to grow or anything over a few minutes a week, you will need a paid plan, and the model you pick will matter more than the plan, since a premium video model can eat credits 20 times faster than a basic one.
Pick the cheaper video model for drafts and save the premium model for the final shot.
